items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The code is well organised, with section banners and Chinese comments on pricing rules and tx. But business logic is full of single-letter names: `var S`, `f = findVariant(sku)`, `l`, `c`, `o`, `r`, `q`, `t`, `fr`, `pv`. The single-letter cap applies.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Everything is in one ~1550-line file, which hits the >500-line cap. The single delegated `document.addEventListener('click', …)` switch handles every action (export, import, reset, rf-restock, refund, …) and is well over 100 lines. Core/quote/tx separation is good, but the cap applies.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: `persist(){ try{ localStorage.setItem(...) } catch(e){ /* 存储不可用时忽略 */ } }` silently drops save failures on every mutation path. `wrap` and `export` also use empty catches. tx rollback and input validation (`isPosInt`, `normQty`) are solid, but the swallowed-mutation-error cap applies.

items.name: Clerk workbench usability: amount breakdown, status hints, dangerous-action confirmation
items.name_zh: 店员工作台可用性：金额明细、状态提示与危险操作确认
items.evidence: Discounts are itemised with labels ('会员 95 折', coupon name/code), plus the coupon shortfall ('还差'), stacking rules and a refund preview. Pay, ship, cancel, refund, restock, import and reset all open confirmBox with plain-language warnings. Status badges and per-status actions are shown, and toasts/alerts give feedback.

items.name: Business logic lives in one place (UI and test API share it; integer-cent money)
items.name_zh: 业务逻辑集中且被界面与测试接口共用（金额按分计算）
items.evidence: shopTestAPI calls `Core.*` directly, the same functions the UI uses. Money is stored in integer cents (`toC`/`toY`, `Math.round`). Stats come from `Core.stats()` computed from orders each time. Import goes through `parseImport`/validation before anything is replaced, and tx snapshots and rolls back on failure.
